title: Unverified Claim That Trump Fired Three Sentencing Commissioners
description_medium: The supplied record says Trump fired three U.S. Sentencing Commission members on January 20, 2025, but its linked source is only the Commission’s general press-release page and does not document such dismissals. At the Commission’s January 24 meeting, Chair Carlton Reeves said two judges’ service had ended earlier that month; the transcript lists five voting commissioners present. The event described in the title is therefore unverified.
evidence_notes: Checked the linked USSC press release index, the January 24, 2025 official meeting transcript, and the Commission’s official description. The transcript says Judges Claria Horn Boom and John Gleeson’s service ended earlier in January, not that Trump fired three members on January 20; it lists five voting commissioners at the meeting.
corrected_wording: No evidence supports that Trump fired three Sentencing Commission members on January 20; the contemporaneous USSC transcript describes two judges' service as having ended earlier that month.
exact_blocker: The claim of three Trump firings on January 20 is not supported by the supplied USSC press-release index and conflicts with the January 24 USSC transcript, which says two members' service ended earlier in January and lists five voting members. A contemporaneous dismissal notice or reliable reporting identifying the alleged three members is needed to substantiate the event.

title: Pentagon Directs Elimination of DEI Offices and Initiatives
description_medium: On January 29, 2025, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued departmentwide guidance directing the Pentagon to eliminate diversity, equity, and inclusion offices and initiatives. The memorandum followed President Trump’s January 27 executive order, “Restoring America’s Fighting Force,” and told senior Defense Department leaders to carry out the policy. A task force was later assigned to assess implementation. The official materials establish the directive, not the record’s claims about abolished equal-opportunity programs or resulting discrimination.
description_long:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s January 29, 2025 memorandum, “Restoring America’s Fighting Force,” directed Defense Department leaders to eliminate offices and initiatives related to diversity, equity, and inclusion. The directive followed President Donald Trump’s January 27 executive order of the same name. The Pentagon described the effort as part of a broader shift toward what the administration called merit-based standards and later created a task force to assess implementation across the department.

This was a departmentwide policy instruction with potential effects on staffing, training, and programs, but the supplied official record does not establish that all equal-opportunity programs dating to military integration were dismantled, that all training materials were removed, or that promotion processes were changed as the original summary claimed. Nor does the directive alone demonstrate that discrimination increased or that unit cohesion was harmed. The supported event is the order to eliminate DEI offices and initiatives, together with the Pentagon’s stated implementation process; specific operational effects require separate evidence.
evidence_notes: Used DoD’s directive and task-force materials. Corrected event date to the January 29 guidance and scoped claims to the formal instruction and described implementation; no supplied source supports claims about removal of all equal-opportunity programs or resulting discrimination.
corrected_wording: The January 29 Hegseth memorandum directed elimination of DEI offices and initiatives; specific claims about all military equal-opportunity programs or consequences are not established by these records.

title: DOJ Appoints Special Counsel Jack Smith
description_medium: On November 18, 2022, Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed veteran prosecutor Jack Smith as special counsel to oversee two ongoing federal investigations involving Donald Trump. One concerned efforts to interfere with the transfer of power after the 2020 election and certification of the Electoral College vote; the other concerned classified documents and possible obstruction. Garland cited the sensitivity of the matters and the presidential campaigns underway as reasons for an independent appointment.
description_long:
Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Jack Smith as special counsel on November 18, 2022, assigning him to oversee two ongoing Justice Department investigations. The first examined whether any person or entity unlawfully interfered with the transfer of power after the 2020 presidential election or with certification of the Electoral College vote on January 6, 2021. The second concerned classified documents and other presidential records held at Donald Trump’s Florida residence, as well as possible obstruction of that investigation.

Garland said the appointment served the public interest given the investigations’ sensitivity and the fact that Trump had announced another presidential campaign while President Joe Biden had said he intended to run again. Smith, a career prosecutor with prior experience at the Justice Department and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, received authority to continue the investigations and prosecute federal crimes arising from them. The appointment itself was an administrative decision about investigative oversight; it was not a finding of guilt or a conclusion about whether charges should be brought. Garland said Smith would exercise independent prosecutorial judgment under DOJ regulations.
evidence_notes: Used Garland’s contemporaneous DOJ remarks, which specify both scopes of investigation and his stated reason for the appointment.

title: Trump Corporation and Trump Payroll Corp. Convicted of 17 Felonies
description_medium: On December 6, 2022, a New York jury convicted the Trump Corporation and Trump Payroll Corp. on all counts in a criminal tax-fraud case brought by the Manhattan district attorney. The verdict covered 17 felony counts involving scheme to defraud, conspiracy, tax fraud, and falsifying business records. Prosecutors said executives received compensation through unreported personal expenses. The companies were the defendants; Donald Trump was not convicted in this case.
description_long:
On December 6, 2022, a New York State Supreme Court jury convicted two Trump Organization entities—the Trump Corporation and the Trump Payroll Corp.—on every count in a Manhattan criminal tax-fraud prosecution. Together, the companies were found guilty of 17 felony counts, including scheme to defraud, conspiracy, criminal tax fraud, and falsifying business records. The Manhattan district attorney said the scheme involved executives receiving compensation through personal expenses that the companies did not properly report to tax authorities.

The case focused on corporate accounting and tax reporting over a period prosecutors described as 13 years. Chief Financial Officer Allen Weisselberg had pleaded guilty separately and testified at trial. The verdict was against the two corporations, not Donald Trump personally; he was not charged in this trial. The distinction is important because headlines calling the defendant simply “the Trump Organization” can obscure which legal entities were convicted and who was not. The jury’s verdict established the companies’ criminal liability on the charged counts, while any separate civil or individual matters require their own records.
evidence_notes: Replaced the unrelated USA Today story with contemporaneous Manhattan DA and New York Attorney General records. Corrected the legal entities and made clear Donald Trump was not a defendant in the corporate trial.
corrected_wording: The jury convicted the Trump Corporation and Trump Payroll Corp. on 17 felony counts; the verdict did not convict Donald Trump personally.

title: Trump Calls Media 'Enemy of the American People' in 2017 Tweet
description_medium: On February 17, 2017, President Donald Trump tweeted that several news organizations were “the enemy of the American People.” The Committee to Protect Journalists identified this as his first use of the phrase on Twitter and documented its later repetition in posts. The title’s claim that he used this exact phrase more than 100 times is unsupported: a 2024 Reporters Without Borders count of 108 referred to public attacks on the media during an eight-week campaign period, not uses of this phrase.
description_long:
On February 17, 2017, President Donald Trump posted a tweet calling several named news organizations “the enemy of the American People.” The Committee to Protect Journalists traced his first use of the phrase on Twitter to that date and found that he used the label four times in tweets during 2017 and 21 times in 2018. CPJ’s analysis treated the phrase as part of a wider pattern of negative rhetoric about the press, including accusations of bias and “fake news.”

The wording mattered because a president was describing news organizations as enemies rather than simply disputing a particular report. Press-freedom advocates warned that repeated attacks could encourage hostility toward journalists; CPJ documented some reporters who said they were harassed after being singled out online. The record’s original “over 100 times” wording overstates evidence about this exact phrase. Reporters Without Borders later counted 108 public verbal attacks on media over an eight-week period in 2024, a different measure that included insults, attacks, or threats in speeches and remarks and excluded social-media posts. The event should therefore be anchored to the specific 2017 tweet, with broader frequency claims carefully qualified.
evidence_notes: Replaced the unrelated White House presidential-actions archive with ABC’s contemporaneous coverage, CPJ’s tweet analysis, and RSF’s later methodology. Corrected the title’s conflation of 108 public attacks in eight weeks with uses of the exact phrase.
corrected_wording: One documented event is Trump’s February 17, 2017 tweet; CPJ counts 25 uses of the exact phrase in tweets through January 2019, while RSF’s 108 counted broader public attacks in a distinct 2024 period.
